FILE ACCESS: your declared outputs are in your worktree and you MAY read and edit them.
Train 2 orchestrator shell guard (tools/shell-writes.mjs). Owner framing: this guard catches orchestrator MISTAKES, it is not a sandbox against attackers; required constructs must be right, exotic ones are recorded and queued, not blockers. Rule the guard must keep: the guard's idea of the current directory must match the shell's at every redirect/write it allows; when it cannot know, it refuses. KNOWN BUG to fix: `( cd docs && true ) && echo x > plans/a.md` is ALLOWED today (orchestratorModeCommandAllowed) although bash restores the directory when the subshell closes, so the write lands at <root>/plans/a.md, outside the allowed area. On origin/main it was refused. Fix omValidateTokenized (~2600+; it already has cwdStack and subshellDepth) so a cd inside ( ... ) is scoped: on the closing ')' restore cwd/local.cwd to the value saved at the matching '('. Do the same for orchestratorSwarmSubfolderBlocked (~1725) if it tracks cd. REQUIRED constructs (each must end with the guard's directory matching the shell's, or be refused): pushd DIR / popd (refuse them unless already refused); ( cd DIR ) subshells (scoped, as above); { cd DIR; } groups (bash keeps the cd, so the cd persists); sh -c / bash -c / zsh -c / eval wrapping a cd plus a redirect (refuse); exec (refuse); builtin cd and command cd (refuse unless handled exactly like cd). Make the product change in tools/shell-writes.mjs only where a required construct is currently allowed AND mismatched. Also cover CDPATH set, cd $VAR / $PWD / $OLDPWD, cd $(...), env cd, time cd: assert today's verdict; if one is allowed AND mismatched, write it with node:test's todo option ('guard gap (queued): <construct>') instead of fixing it, and list it in notes.
